format.consumer: sglang 9e6d1c0 multimodal_gen Fp8Config.from_config (quant_method fp8): weight_block_size -> block quant, BlockQuantScaleParameter named weight_scale_inv
format.scale_semantics: DEQUANTISATION MULTIPLIER despite the DeepSeek-V3 name: W[i, j] ~= float(weight[i, j]) * weight_scale_inv[i // 128, j // 128]
format.activation_semantics: dynamic, per token, per contiguous 128-channel group along the input dimension: s = max(max|x|, 1e-10) / 448, x_q = RNE_E4M3(clamp(x / s, -448, 448)); the semantics every FP8 block-GEMM path of the pinned engine implements (DeepGEMM, CUTLASS blockwise, Triton w8a8_block)
format.rounding: round to nearest, ties to even, onto the finite E4M3 grid; values clamped to +-448 BEFORE the cast (so no NaN code can appear); the sign of a value that rounds to zero is kept (0x80)
format.non_quantized_tensors: byte-identical copies of the source tensors (float16), biases of quantized linears included
format.container: one safetensors file diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors, metadata {"format": "pt"}, plus config.json = the source config with quantization_config added (modules_to_not_convert = every non-quantized module that owns a .weight, sorted)
format.scale_arithmetic: scale = fl32(amax / 448), the correctly rounded float32 quotient, on every device (implemented as a tensor-by-tensor division with a same-shape, same-device divisor). NOT amax * fl32(1/448), which is what a CUDA tensor divided by a Python scalar computes.

algorithm: for each quantized weight W (float16 [N, K]); N and K are multiples of 128 for every SD3-medium target, so no padding block exists
amax[b] = max |W| over each 128x128 block b (exact in float16); an all-zero block is REFUSED (the pinned converter would produce NaN)
scale[b] = fl32(amax[b] / 448): float32 IEEE division by a same-shape, same-device float32 tensor (see format.scale_arithmetic)
q = cast_e4m3fn(clamp(float32(W) / scale[block of each element], -448, 448))  (float32 IEEE division)

operation for operation the same as sglang 9e6d1c0 python/sglang/multimodal_gen/tools/convert_hf_to_fp8.py::block_fp8 EXCEPT the scale division (the converter's is a Python-scalar division, i.e. multiply-by-reciprocal on its hard-coded CUDA device). A GPU build re-derives every tensor on CPU and refuses a mismatch (exit 6).

quantized_modules.rule: every linear of the 24 joint blocks' attention projections (both streams) and feed-forward networks (both streams)
quantized_modules.count_derivation: blocks 0-22: 4 image-attn + 3 context-qkv + to_add_out + 2 ff + 2 ff_context = 12 each (276); block 23 (context_pre_only): 4 + 3 + 2 = 9; total 285
quantized_modules.differs_from_the_pinned_converter: convert_hf_to_fp8.py's name filter skips every key containing 'net', so on SD3 it quantizes the 191 attention projections and leaves all 94 feed-forward linears in 16 bit -- about a third of the per-block GEMM FLOPs. The recipe names its list explicitly instead, and keeps the converter's arithmetic.

high_precision_modules.rule: not quantized, kept as the source's float16: adaLN modulation linears (norm1.linear, norm1_context.linear, norm_out.linear: M = batch rows, conditioning-sensitive), the patch/pos/time/text embedders, context_embedder, proj_out; all norms, softmax, GELU and the attention core (QK^T, PV) run in 16/32-bit as the engine normally does
high_precision_modules.note: FP8 attention (QK^T/PV in FP8) is out of scope for this recipe

randomness: none: the recipe is a pure function of the source bytes; there is no seed to fix

libraries.note: reference conversion versions; the generated manifest records the versions actually used

identity.content: tensor_set_sha256 = sha256 over the sorted lines 'name<TAB>dtype<TAB>shape<TAB>sha256(raw bytes)'. This is the identity the benchmark relies on: it does not depend on how the container lays the tensors out.
identity.container: file_sha256 of diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors and config.json, recorded separately; a different safetensors version may reorder the header without changing a single tensor, and that is reported as container drift, not as a different asset
identity.recipe_fingerprint: sha256 over the NORMATIVE fields listed in sd3_fp8_recipe.py (source sha/file/n_tensors, quantization_config, dtypes, scale suffix, scale_arithmetic, include_regex, expected_count); prose edits do not change it

expected.measured: The expected hashes describe a CPU conversion using torch 2.9.1+cu128, safetensors 0.8.0 and numpy 2.3.5. Copied tensors retain the source bytes. CUDA conversions must pass the converter's independent CPU cross-check.
expected.per_tensor: Per-tensor hashes are recorded in the generated fp8_manifest.json.
